title: mesh_outbound_registry plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `mesh_outbound_registry` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component MeshOutboundRegistryConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

MeshOutboundRegistryConfig.description:
Plugin: mesh_outbound_registry — Implements Istio
`outboundTrafficPolicy.mode: REGISTRY_ONLY`. Rejects HTTP
requests whose `Host` header is not in the configured destination
registry. Auto-injected by mesh mode when the EFFECTIVE outbound policy
resolves to `RegistryOnly` — workload-scoped
`Sidecar.outboundTrafficPolicy`, else mesh-wide
`MeshConfig.outboundTrafficPolicy`, else
`FERRUM_MESH_OUTBOUND_TRAFFIC_POLICY`; not registered when the effective
policy is `AllowAny` (default).
Operator-managed instances on non-mesh gateways behave as a generic
HTTP `Host` allowlist.

Matches against four kinds of entries: bare hostnames (no Host port),
explicit `host:port` pairs, `host:*` (any explicit Host port), and
wildcard hosts (`*.example.com`, `*.example.com:443`,
`*.example.com:*`). Empty registry fails closed. Request `Host`
ports use the registry grammar (decimal 1–65535); `:0`, signed, or
non-numeric ports are denied. Mesh-derived registries drop slice
hosts outside this grammar with a warning (they stay denied) instead
of failing the whole config; operator-authored entries stay strict.
Denials log a rate-limited warning naming the denied host.

registry.description:
Known destinations. Bare hostnames match requests with no
explicit `Host` port. `host:port` entries match only that port.
`host:*` entries match any explicit port. Wildcard entries
(`*.example.com[:port|:*]`) match per `wildcard_match` (one
DNS label below the suffix by default). Hostname labels use ASCII letters, digits, and interior
hyphens; supply internationalized names in punycode. IPv4 names
and IPv6 literals are supported; bracket IPv6 when specifying a
numeric port. Bare IPv6 and IPv6:* are also accepted.
Numeric destination ports are decimal 1–65535 (leading zeros
allowed). Surrounding whitespace, hostname case, trailing
hostname dots, and IPv6 spelling are normalized. Empty or
whitespace-only entries are ignored; an empty effective registry
rejects all destinations wherever enforcement applies.
URLs, paths, userinfo, internal whitespace, malformed brackets,
misplaced wildcards, and invalid ports fail construction with
the zero-based registry entry index.

reject_status.description:
Status code returned for unknown destinations. Operators may
override to 404 to mask unknown destinations.

outbound_listen_ports.description:
Optional frontend listener ports where the registry is enforced.
Every instance skips the listener-stamped Inbound mesh direction
before any registry decision, even on a matching port. Empty means
enforce on every other HTTP-family request, including non-mesh
listeners (operator-managed default). Mesh auto-injection names
the outbound capture listener ports. Ports must be 1–65535; use
`[]` for intentional global scope.

namespace.description:
Value of the mesh_namespace label on
ferrum_mesh_outbound_registry_decisions_total. Mesh injection
explicitly supplies the runtime namespace. Direct instances use
this config value (default ferrum), independently of the enclosing
PluginConfig resource namespace.

wildcard_match.description:
How `*.suffix` registry entries match request hosts.
`one_label` (default) matches exactly one DNS label below the
suffix (`api.example.com`, not `a.b.example.com`); this is the
Ferrum mesh wildcard contract shared with Sidecar egress scoping,
the mesh DNS proxy, and the stream-family REGISTRY_ONLY lane, so
mesh auto-injection always uses it. `dns_suffix` matches any DNS
name below the suffix (`a.b.example.com` too), like Envoy
virtual-host domains and Istio's host matcher. The base domain
never matches either mode. In `dns_suffix` mode an authority
over 253 bytes or with an empty label never matches a wildcard,
and probing stops at the deepest configured suffix's label
count.
